name: Nova
behaviour: Asks a short follow-up question and pushes back once before accepting an explanation
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of OOP and its importance in programming
Learn to define classes and objects in Java
Understand the difference between classes and objects
Be able to create objects and use their methods
Understand the concept of inheritance and polymorphism

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Students may think that OOP is only about creating objects
misconceptions.correct_concept: OOP is a programming paradigm that organizes programs as a collection of objects, each representing an instance of a class, and whose classes are all members of a hierarchy of classes united via inheritance relationships.
misconceptions.reason: Students may form this misconception because they may not fully understand the concept of OOP and its importance in programming. To rectify this, instructors can provide examples of how OOP is used in real-world applications and emphasize its benefits in terms of code reusability and modularity.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Students may think that classes and objects are the same thing
misconceptions.correct_concept: A class is an abstract definition of a data type, including data elements and operations, while an object is a specific instance of a class.
misconceptions.reason: Students may form this misconception because they may not fully understand the difference between classes and objects. To rectify this, instructors can provide examples of how classes and objects are used in different contexts and emphasize the importance of understanding the relationship between the two.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Students may think that OOP is only about creating objects and methods
misconceptions.correct_concept: OOP is also about encapsulation, abstraction, and inheritance, which allow for more complex systems to be developed using smaller, independent subsystems.
misconceptions.reason: Students may form this misconception because they may not fully understand the scope of OOP and its benefits. To rectify this, instructors can provide examples of how OOP is used in different contexts and emphasize its importance in terms of code reusability and modularity.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Students may think that OOP is only for Java or C++
misconceptions.correct_concept: OOP is a programming paradigm that can be applied to any programming language that supports object-oriented programming.
misconceptions.reason: Students may form this misconception because they may not fully understand the scope of OOP and its applicability to different programming languages. To rectify this, instructors can provide examples of how OOP is used in different programming languages and emphasize its importance in terms of code reusability and modularity.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Students may think that polymorphism only refers to method overriding
misconceptions.correct_concept: Polymorphism refers to the ability of an object to take on multiple forms, including method overriding, method overloading, and operator overloading.
misconceptions.reason: Students may form this misconception because they may not fully understand the concept of polymorphism and its different forms. To rectify this, instructors can provide examples of how polymorphism is used in different contexts and emphasize its importance in terms of code reusability and modularity.
